text: Japan buys crude oil from the Persian Gulf, iron ore from Western Australia and LNG from Qatar. Research the three shipping routes separately, and tell me which narrow strait the Gulf crude and the Qatari LNG tankers both have to pass through on the way out.

delegated.summary: Crude from Gulf terminals leaves the Persian Gulf through the Strait of Hormuz, crosses the Arabian Sea and the Indian Ocean, and passes the Strait of Malacca before reaching Japan.

findings.claim: Tankers leaving the Persian Gulf pass the Strait of Hormuz, the waterway between the Persian Gulf and the Gulf of Oman

delegated.summary: LNG from Ras Laffan loads inside the Persian Gulf and leaves through the Strait of Hormuz.

findings.claim: Ras Laffan, Qatar, is on the Persian Gulf coast; its LNG carriers leave via the Strait of Hormuz
